title: SECTION 15: IMPORTANT ACTS, LAWS & LEGAL FRAMEWORK

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Public Order and Police are state subjects under Entries 1 and 2 of List II in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India.
Karnataka-Specific Legislation, such as the Karnataka Police Act of 1963, provides the legal framework for police force regulation and law maintenance in the state.

Central Laws including the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and special central acts form the core legal framework for competitive exams like Police Sub-Inspector (PSI) and KPSC.
Constitutional safeguards like Article 22 protect individuals against arbitrary arrest and detention, mandating production before a magistrate within 24 hours.

blocks.content: Constitutional Provisions Related to Police & Public Order

cells: Defines police structure; DGP as head; powers of SI (register FIR, investigate, arrest); Section 20 — general police duties; Section 27 — disperse unlawful assembly; Section 34 — prohibitory orders
Anti-corruption ombudsman; Lokayukta & 2 Upa-Lokayuktas; jurisdiction over all public servants except Governor & CM while in office; cannot impose penalties
Implements 73rd Amendment; Zilla Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat, Gram Panchayat; 1/3 reservation for women; Gram Sabha powers
Governs city corporations; BBMP, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Belagavi, Kalaburagi, Davanagere, Shivamogga corporations
Tenancy abolition; land to tiller; ceiling on landholding; major agrarian reform; cannot sell agricultural land to non-farmers
Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter & Preservation of Animals Act
Strict ban on cow slaughter; penalty up to 7 years; bovine animal protection
Stamp duty rates on various instruments; property transfer
Karnataka Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
Implements SC/ST (PoA) Act; district-level protection committees; special courts
Combat organised crime gangs; extended remand; rigorous investigation powers; inspired by MCOCA (Maharashtra)
Time-bound delivery of government services; officers penalised for delay; first state in South India to pass such law
Transparent procurement; e-tendering; Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurement Rules 2000
Regulates private schools; fee regulation; medium of instruction; government school norms
Labour safety in factories; relevant for industrial districts
Working hours, holidays, leave for commercial establishment employees

rows: Regulates the police force structure, duties, and public order maintenance within Karnataka.
Defines criminal offences, trial procedures, and rules of evidence applicable across India.
Establishes legislative power over police and provides fundamental constitutional safeguards to detainees.

blocks.content: 15.2 Central Laws — Critical for SI/PSC Exams

cells: Replaced IPC; 358 sections; new provisions for organised crime (S.111), terrorism (S.113), community service punishment; sedition removed; trial in absentia
Replaced CrPC; Zero FIR (S.173); e-FIR; mandatory forensic team for serious offences; extended remand up to 60 days; video conferencing trials
Replaced Indian Evidence Act; electronic records as primary evidence (S.63); digital documents; confession rules retained
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences; special courts; mandatory reporting; rigorous punishment; recent amendments enhanced penalties
Prohibit atrocities; special courts; anticipatory bail restricted; public humiliation as offence; designated courts
Narcotic Drugs & Psychotropic Substances; no bail for commercial quantity; asset attachment; NDPS courts; major enforcement responsibility for police
Licensing of firearms; prohibited categories; Kodavas of Karnataka specifically exempted (can carry traditional weapons without licence)
Traffic enforcement; 2019 amendment: enhanced fines (helmet Rs.1000, drunk driving Rs.10,000, speeding Rs.5000 repeat); good samaritans protected
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence; Protection Officer; Magistrate can issue Protection & Residence Orders
Prevention of Money Laundering; ED as enforcement agency; proceeds of crime attachment; police coordinate with ED
Right to Information; Public Information Officers; SIC (State Information Commission Karnataka); 30-day reply deadline
Children in conflict with law; 16–18 heinous offences can be tried as adults (Juvenile Justice Board decides); child care institutions
Protected species schedules; penalties for poaching; National Board for Wildlife; recent amendments stiffen penalties
Tribal and forest dwellers' rights; Soliga tribe used this to secure their rights in BRT Tiger Reserve (Supreme Court landmark judgment)

items: Seventh Schedule Division: Direct questions frequently ask for the specific entries of 'Police' (Entry 2) and 'Public Order' (Entry 1) under the State List.
Arrest Rights: Article 22(2) mandates that every person who is arrested and detained in custody must be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours.
Central Laws Overhaul: Candidates must be well-versed with the modern replacements of substantive and procedural criminal laws critical for SI and PSC examinations.

blocks.content: 15.3 Constitutional Provisions Related to Police & Public Order

cells: Police & Public Order = State List (Entry 1 & 2); Criminal Law = Concurrent List (Entry 1)
Protect against internal disturbance; basis for deploying central forces
In case of failure of constitutional machinery; state police comes under central direction
Special provisions; educational & employment reservations for local candidates in Bidar, Kalaburagi, Raichur, Yadgir, Koppal, Vijayanagara districts
Grounds of arrest communicated; lawyer access; magistrate within 24 hours; 44th Amendment — right to be informed
Habeas Corpus — release from illegal detention; most important writ for police accountability
Deployment in Karnataka during elections, emergencies; DM can requisition
